text:
Rohan: quick postmortem from the meridianX int6-ish trial on long narratives — good unit-econ but a reproducible degradation on table/ledger-like prompts
Priya: can you summarize the econ numbers and the failure mode?
Rohan: econ: token_cost baseline fp16 =~ $0.019/1k -> int6 =~ $0.011/1k (~42% saving). Traffic-weighted monthly delta ~ $9.2k for the pilot route. Perf: p95 latency +6% under steady-state batching. Failures: structured extraction + entity co-ref errors on multi-doc inputs
Ilya: interesting. is the failure rate concentrated or diffuse? any common tokens/priming?
Rohan: concentrated. We sliced GTN long-narrative set by presence of dense 2+ column tables and repeated aliases. Failure rate on that slice rose from 2.1% -> 7.9% (abs +5.8%)
Jess: that's meaningful. product will be sensitive if that slice is high-value. Can we narrow which mechanism is causing it? quant noise in cross-attn? kv-cache alignment?
Ilya: hypothesis: quantized softmax and small negative logits near boundaries are flipping argmax for entity tokens. Another possibility is our fused kv-cache read path dropping precision on very long context windows
Rohan: ran a local debug: compared attention-weight distributions FP16 vs INT6 for a failing example. saw heavier tail mass in int6 and slightly higher entropy around cross-attn steps near doc boundaries
Priya: ok. what are mitigation options? we need an ops-friendly plan that preserves most savings but protects the slice
Jess: options brainstorm: 1) deterministic routing by a classifier: classify long inputs with tables -> route to fp16 2) lightweight patch: increase kv-cache slot precision for flagged routes 3) staged fallback: shadow -> sample -> fallback on coherence fail 4) prompt-transform: chunk & re-encode with explicit entity markers
Ilya: for (2) we could enable a hybrid kernel that keeps KV as float16 while the rest stays int6. cost hit small but may fix the tail. Need bench to quantify
Rohan: I prototyped a classifier (tiny transformer) that flags table-like inputs with 95% recall / 88% precision on our GTN holdout. cheap to run (<2ms) and high recall so it's viable for routing
Priya: product asks for an automated policy rather than manual monitoring. Jess, can you draft a routing policy that balances risk?
Jess: propose: start with shadowing + canary rollout:
```
policy {
  name: meridianx-selective-precision
  classifier: table_detector_v1
  shadow_route: meridianX-13B-fp16 (shadow_sample_rate=0.05)
  canary_route: meridianX-13B-fp16 (sample_rate=0.02)
  default_route: meridianX-13B-int6
  fallback_on: coherence_fail || entity_mismatch
  metrics: {coherence, entity_f1, p95_latency, unit_cost}
}
```
Rohan: love it. let's add an automatic rollback rule: if coherence delta > 3 pts on 5k sampled canary -> rollback and route to fp16 for that classifier bucket
Ilya: also suggest a micro-benchmark to test the hybrid-kv idea: run 1k examples with kv-float16 + int6 compute, measure coherence and cost delta. If it fixes >80% of failures with <15% cost increase relative to int6, it might be preferred to full fp16
Priya: timeline: Jess to implement policy + dashboard tiles; Rohan to run hybrid-kv micro-bench; Ilya to run 5k shadow evaluation; I'll coordinate product review and decide acceptable thresholds
Jess: I'll add a logging tag `precision_route` and include `predictor_tag` from the classifier. Also emit `unit_cost_estimate` per response so dashboards can compute weighted economics
infra-bot: Scheduled job created: meridianx-hybrid-kv-bench (1k) -> runs at 2026-03-24T02:00:00Z
Rohan: for the 5k shadow eval I'll use: s3://redwood-eval/meridianx/long-narrative-shadow/5k.jsonl and eval harness path /evals/long-coherence-v2. Expect results in ~8h
Ilya: I'll prepare the gating signal code: `coherence_fail` defined as coherence_score drop >= 0.03 AND entity_f1 drop >= 0.04 compared to fp16 baseline
Priya: product note: if the failing slice is under 3% of monthly revenue and we can save >35% on unit price, product is willing to accept up to 4pt coherence drop but only if we have gradual rollout and quick rollback automation
Jess: ops note: pre-warm plan for fp16 fallback: autoscale_min=2 for canary and shadow pool, add alert on p95 latency + 15% within 10 minutes
Rohan: follow-ups I will post: 1) micro-bench results + logs 2) initial 5k shadow metrics 3) cost projections for 30/60/90 days at various routing splits (90/10, 95/5, 98/2)
Ilya: +1. also will dump attention diffs for top 20 failing prompts to help diagnostics
Priya: thanks team. any objections to proceeding with the shadow -> canary -> staged rollout plan?
Jess: no objections from infra side
Rohan: go ahead, will report back with morning update
Priya: agreed. product greenlight pending the first shadow eval.
